incidente.resumo: A bug in the Google Cloud HTTP(S) Load Balancer configuration update process caused load balancers to revert to a substantially out-of-date configuration, and requests experienced a 25% error rate (502 errors) for 22 minutes, with some recently modified load balancers at 100%. Engineers mitigated it by switching the configuration update process to a different master server.

descricao.texto: Google engineers were paged at 01:22 PDT.
trechos: Google engineers were paged at 01:22 PDT.

gatilho.texto: One of the replicas of the master servers that control the configuration update process lost access to Google's distributed file system and could not read recent configuration files; mastership then passed to that server.
trechos: The configuration update process is controlled by a master server.
In this case, one of the replicas of the master servers lost access to Google's distributed file system and was unable to read recent configuration files.
Mastership then passed to the server that could not access Google's distributed file system.

descricao.texto: A bug in the HTTP(S) Load Balancer configuration update process: when a new master's test push fails, it reverts all load balancers to the last "known good" configuration, which here was the latest configuration that master could read and was substantially out of date.
trechos: A bug in the HTTP(S) Load Balancer configuration update process caused it to revert to a configuration that was substantially out of date.
If the test fails (as it did in this case), the new master will revert all HTTP(S) Load Balancers to the last "known good" configuration.

The combination of a mastership change, lack of access to more recent updates, and the initial test failure for the latest config caused the HTTP(S) Load Balancers to revert to the latest configuration that the master could read, which was substantially out-of-date.

fatores_contribuintes.texto: The out-of-date configuration update triggered garbage collection on the Google Frontend servers to free memory used by the deleted configurations; the high number of deleted configurations made them spend a large share of CPU on garbage collection, which led to failed health checks and restarts, and requests served by a restarting server received 502 errors.
trechos: In addition, the update with the out-of-date configuration triggered a garbage collection process on the Google Frontend servers to free up memory used by the deleted configurations.

The high number of deleted configurations caused the Google Frontend servers to spend a large proportion of CPU cycles on garbage collection which lead to failed health checks and eventual restart of the affected Google Frontend server.
Any client requests served by a restarting server received 502 errors.

passos.texto: At 01:34 engineers switched the configuration update process to use a different master server, which mitigated the issue for most services within one minute.
trechos: They switched the configuration update process to use a different master server at 01:34 which mitigated the issue for most services within one minute.

acoes.texto: Planned: master servers will be configured to never push HTTP(S) Load Balancer configurations that are more than a few hours old.
trechos: Master servers will be configured to never push HTTP(S) Load Balancer configurations that are more than a few hours old.

acoes.texto: Planned: Google Frontend servers will reject loading a configuration file that is more than a few hours old.
trechos: Google Frontend servers will reject loading a configuration file that is more than a few hours old.

acoes.texto: Planned: improve testing for new HTTP(S) Load Balancer configurations so that out-of-date configurations are flagged before being pushed to production.
trechos: Improve testing for new HTTP(S) Load Balancer configurations so that out-of-date configurations are flagged before being pushed to production.

acoes.texto: Planned: fix the issue that caused the master server to fail when reading files from Google's distributed file system.
trechos: Fix the issue that caused the master server to fail when reading files from Google's distributed file system.

acoes.texto: Planned: fix the issue that caused health check failures on Google Frontends during heavy garbage collection.
trechos: Fix the issue that caused health check failures on Google Frontends during heavy garbage collection.
On Wednesday 5 April 2017, requests to the Google Cloud HTTP(S) Load Balancer experienced a 25% error rate for a duration of 22 minutes.

observacoes: The document is a status-page incident entry with a single update containing the post-mortem, so tipo is atualizacoes_status. After the incident, configuration changes to the HTTP(S) Load Balancer were paused for three hours and 41 minutes (until 05:16) while the root cause was confirmed, which caused App Engine Flexible app deployments to fail during that period.
